mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over the last two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST shows a sustained increase over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% over the last month signals a contraction in supply, which increases prices and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS grew by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the last month, it signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within the last month, signals strong economic growth and a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases over last quarter and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: economic expansion with tight labor market
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where GDPC1 increased over the last quarter and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% within the last month.
